answers.answer: The supplied source is titled “Helical phases and Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces probed by superconducting diode effects,” by Zekun Zhuang, Daniel Shaffer, Jaglul Hasan, and Alex Levchenko. It contains only \date{\today}; no arXiv identifier, version number, submission date, or revision date is present. Equivalence to arXiv:2510.18963 and its PDF version/date therefore remains unresolved from this source alone.

The literal original-TeX self-consistency equation is
\[\Delta \ln \frac{T}{T_c}+\pi T\sum_{\omega_n>0,\lambda}\left[\frac{\Delta}{\omega_n}-(1+\lambda\tilde{\alpha})\langle i(g_\lambda)_{12}\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}\right]=0.\]
Thus the first term is exactly \(\Delta\ln(T/T_c)\), and the bracket contains \(\Delta/\omega_n\) minus \((1+\lambda\tilde\alpha)\langle i(g_\lambda)_{12}\rangle_{\rm FS}\), with the overall prefactor \(\pi T\).

The extracted scalar expression \(T\ln(T/T_c)+2\pi T\sum(1/\omega_n-1/\Omega_n)=0\) is not the literal source equation and is dimensionally inconsistent when \(T,\omega_n,\Omega_n\) are energies. The source equation is dimensionally consistent: each bracket term has inverse-energy dimension, and \(\pi T\) supplies energy; \(\Delta\ln(T/T_c)\) also has energy dimension. The likely issue is extraction/algebraic misreading: dividing the source equation by \(\Delta\), then taking the zero-field equal-band homogeneous limit, yields \(\ln(T/T_c)+2\pi T\sum_{\omega_n>0}(1/\omega_n-1/\Omega_n)=0\), not a prefactor \(T\) multiplying the logarithm.

The canonical physical BCS self-consistency implied by the supplied Hamiltonian and the stated \(T_c\) regularization is the source equation itself, with \(i(g_\lambda)_{12}=\Delta_\lambda/\Omega_\lambda\) in the homogeneous solution. In the zero-field, zero-momentum, equal-gap limit this reduces after division by \(\Delta\) to \(\ln(T/T_c)+2\pi T\sum_{\omega_n>0}[1/\omega_n-1/\sqrt{\omega_n^2+\Delta^2}]=0\). No prospective physics correction is required; the extracted scalar should be corrected to this form.

The endpoint description is: at low temperature \(j(q)\) has a local minimum; as temperature increases that minimum becomes an inflection point at \(T_{\rm CEP}\), ending the first-order transition. The source separately states equilibrium is selected by \(j(q)=0\). Under the usual smooth coalescence of the minimum and neighboring branch, the stationary zero-current CEP conditions \(j=j'=j''=0\) follow as an inference: \(j=0\) from equilibrium, while coalescence of stationary branches gives \(j'=0\) and their merger/inflection gives \(j''=0\). The derivative notation is not explicitly printed in the source, so these conditions should be flagged as an inferred mathematical characterization, not as a missing literal equation.
